The view's section count is the compiler's structural fact (every Section reachable from the root's children without crossing another Section), so neither a nested section of a section nor a wrapper container can change the count the shape rule reads. The closure removes orphan dependents: every read of a retained need is retained transitively, so no retained behavior depends on a dropped one, and the contract lane's closed-read assertion proves it over both projection plans. The fixpoint is that invariant's own guard as well as the rule's own statement: for a decodable plan the closure already retains every read a retained need names, so the guard cannot fire and its refusal is not claimed as exercised. A read that names an input or constant is not a dropped behavior. The disclosure is emitted into the composition before admission, coverage and the gap writer, so it survives a writer that succeeds: the packaged chat mode fills one retained need from the catalogue, writes the rest through a gap section, and the accepted experience is that writer's own authored field carrying the omission notice beside the labelled Tabs root, so neither the disclosure nor the writer's candidate can be a fallback artifact. A whole custom chat draft at the frozen chat target - the chat route is never classified, so that draft is the ordinary whole writing, and a whole draft is the composition's only content - is refused before emission when it carries a header or hero or more than two sections, authorizing a source repair; the same rule reads an edited draft's emitted view, so an accepted pair edited into a header is source feedback for the next ask and the previous draft stays. The specification's 'compact' clause is enforced as that whole-chat shape (headerless and at most two sections): the style token 'compact' is a Column/Row/List/Grid style and no container style is mandated for a whole chat by this sentence. The rule is scoped to the whole chat the specification constrains, so a gap section written beside an existing composition is not a whole chat.
